note: Gathered and written by a machine from public sources and checked against them. Not reviewed by a person, not rights-cleared, not tested on learners. The rules are in manifest.json.

card.name: Al-Ayyala
card.profile: Two rows of ~20 men with thin bamboo canes (as spears) face each other while drummers between play; men sway heads and sticks and chant poetry, simulating battle. Joint Oman/UAE, UNESCO 2014. Composite performing art (poetry+drum+dance).

observation.setting: Public outdoor and indoor ceremonial spaces, likely official or festive events.
observation.dancers: Mixed group; men in lines, women in front of the men.
observation.formation_and_space: Men stand in two parallel lines facing each other; women stand in a line in front of the men.
observation.posture: Men stand upright with torso held straight; women stand upright with torso slightly leaning forward during hair flips.
observation.footwork: Men perform rhythmic, synchronized stepping in place or moving slightly forward; women's footwork is minimal or stationary.
observation.arms_and_hands: Men hold swords or bamboo sticks vertically or horizontally; women hold their hair or let it hang loose to flip it.
observation.hips_and_torso: Men's torsos are relatively still; women perform vigorous torso and head movements to flip their hair.
observation.partnering: None; the groups perform in parallel lines.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Mostly standing level; no jumps or floor work observed.
observation.costume_and_props: Men wear traditional white thobes and headgear, holding swords or sticks; women wear traditional dresses and have long hair.
observation.cannot_infer: Specific footwork details are obscured by the long garments and camera angles; exact rhythmic precision is difficult to determine due to video editing.

signature_moments.what: Men in two lines holding swords and moving in unison.
Women in front of the men performing synchronized hair flips.
Close-up of women flipping their hair to the beat.
